Macrons

Consonantal i

Travel & transport

pack verb

classical

Traupman 217

sarcinās colligere

Examples

  • Avus et avia, quī in cubiculō proximō dormīverant, sarcinīs collēctīs parātī in vestibulō exspectābant. Ratiōne putātā ā dēversōriō discessum est.

    Grandpa and Grandma, who had slept in the next room, had packed and were waiting ready in the lobby. The bill was settled and they checked out.Libellus VI, Reditus: per Alpēs domum

See also luggage, check out.

SourcesJohn C. Traupman, Conversational Latin for Oral Proficiency: p. 217, checked against the searchable text of the book on 29 October 2026.

Theodōrus et pater · Ad Larem avītum, Libellī I–VII, as they stood on 7 November 2026, with their glosses. Examples marked “Libellus” quote those texts word for word; classical passages are cited by author.
